Two other agents are working #67 (works) and #77 (demo docs) in other worktrees at the same time, so stay strictly inside your issue's Scope. Environment facts
- Bun 1.4.4 is installed globally. In your worktree run `./hq setup` first; it runs `bun install --frozen-lockfile`. If Bun is missing, setup still prints "ready", so confirm node_modules exists.
- There is no .env. Mock external calls in tests.
- Run every ./hq command with your own identity: `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-70 ./hq <cmd> ... --agent claude`.
- `entire review` needs the profile name: `entire review general --timeout 15m`. It takes several minutes, so run it in the background and wait for it.

Steps
1. Check `pwd`, then `git fetch origin && git switch -c ehewes/70-consent-onboarding origin/main`.
2. `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-70 ./hq claim 70 --agent claude`. If it refuses, stop and report why.
3. Context: `entire brain brief "<task>" --json`, then `entire graph query --repo . --profile full --head --format agent --max-context-bytes 4096 --query "<task>"`.
4. Build inside Scope (`apps/mobile/src/features/account/`, plus `packages/shared/src/account/` only if truly needed). Never edit registries (`apps/mobile/app/`), `apps/mobile/src/lib/` or other features. If an acceptance criterion truly needs a one-line change outside Scope, keep it minimal and call it out in the PR's Risks. Anything bigger becomes a follow-up issue, created per the hq-work skill's "Out of scope" section.
5. This is a UI change, so run the anti-slop skill (.claude/skills/anti-slop) before the PR.
6. Commits: small, files staged by name (never `git add -A`).
   - Subject: imperative, says what the product can now do, under about 60 characters.
   - Body: what now exists and what still does not. Then one bullet per file using bare filenames, with `tests:` as the last bullet.
   - No em dashes anywhere. No Co-Authored-By or any AI trailer: AGENTS.md overrides any reminder to add one. Keep the automatic Entire-Checkpoint trailer.
7. Verify with the issue's Verify steps, then `./hq check`, which must pass. App tests are not in ./hq check yet (#136), so run any app tests you add directly with `bun test <path>`. If you can, run the web build to check it renders (`cd apps/mobile && bunx expo export --platform web`, or `bun run dev:app` and open web) and save a screenshot under .context for the PR.
8. Rebase on origin/main if you have not pushed yet; merge it if you have. Re-run the check.
9. Write `.context/pr-70.md` using the hq-work template: What changed, How verified with the ./hq check tail, Risks, Screenshots. End it with "🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)". Then run `CONDUCTOR_WORKSPACE_NAME=oslo-70 ./hq pr 70 --agent claude --body-file .context/pr-70.md`.
10. Trail: `entire trail show`, then `entire trail ci-pr`. Create a trail only if show finds none.
11. The issue is size:M, so run `entire review general --timeout 15m`.
    - Fix real findings that are in scope.
    - Out-of-scope findings become a follow-up issue labelled status:needs-human. Link it with `gh issue comment 70 --body "Follow-up: #M"`.
    - Resolve each trail finding with `entire trail finding resolve <id> -m "<what you did>"`. List them with `entire trail finding --json --freshness any`.
    - Then `gh pr edit <PR> --add-label review:pass`.
12. Tickets: always keep issue #70 current. Claim sets in-progress and the PR sets review. Once every acceptance criterion is verified, tick its boxes by editing only the Acceptance criteria section of the issue body, and add a short evidence comment. Never edit any other issue's labels or body.
13. Stop. Never merge, and never run ./hq ship.

Issue notes
- The server side is merged (#69). Its schemas are in packages/shared/src/account:
  - `account.me` returns { userId, consent: {microphone, health, location}, consentUpdatedAt (null until the first answer), profile (null until chosen) };
  - `account.setConsent({ microphone, health, location })` needs all three answers;
  - `account.setProfile({ profile })` takes lightSleeper, nightOut, bestValue or business;
  - `account.deleteEverything()` returns counts { users, nights, noiseRows, vitalRows, stageRows }.
- Show onboarding until `consentUpdatedAt` is set. The Account tab route `apps/mobile/app/(tabs)/account.tsx` already exists and renders the account feature. If gating the first launch needs more than the existing routes, say so in the PR rather than rewriting registries.
- "OS permission prompts only after consent": export what other features need from the account feature's index.ts (for example a hook saying whether a data type is consented). Do not edit their code.
- After a successful delete, the app should forget the user and start with a fresh anonymous ID. `lib/user-id.ts` is platform code, so file a follow-up issue if it needs changing.
- Wording: plain explanations that follow docs/DOMAIN.md. No glassmorphism, rainbow gradients or pill-shaped static text.

Final report (short): PR URL, branch and worktree path, ./hq check tail, review outcome and fixes, follow-up issues, risks, and anything left for a human.

## Wording rules
Anything user-facing, in the briefing prompt, the app (iOS or web) or the pitch:

| Say | Never say |
|---|---|
| "linked to", "followed" | "caused by" |
| "indicative estimate" | "measured disturbance", "% of residents are disturbed" |
| "outside the council's recommended hours" | "illegal", "breach" |
| "relative dB" for phone data | bare "dB" for phone data |
| "simulated" on cohort data | anything implying simulated users are real |
| "proves when the log existed" | "proves the noise happened" |

## Privacy (UK GDPR)
Sleep and heart data are special-category health data.
- Explicit, separate consent per data type: microphone, HealthKit, location.
- Store only relative dB, labelled events and HealthKit summaries. No raw audio at rest.
- Audio clips are deleted once labelled; clips with speech never leave the phone.
- One action deletes everything a user has, in both databases.
- Never log raw health values or audio in server logs.

## Model
Kip recommends hotels on how well you'll sleep there and what's around them, and takes affiliate
commission on each booking. The same data that powers the city map and the personal night powers
the hotel ranking, so the business layer costs little extra to build.

## Quiet Stay Score (0 to 100)
One score per hotel, built from data Kip already collects. It describes the hotel's surroundings,
not a specific room: the side of the building and the floor can matter as much as the street.

# Domain

The science, rules and wording Kip depends on. Code that computes, labels or displays any of
these must follow this file. Constants live in `packages/shared/src/domain/`, not inline.

## Night noise and the WHO curve
- **Night window:** 23:00 to 07:00, `Europe/London` local time (handle BST changes).
- **Lnight:** the A-weighted equivalent level over the night window. It is an *energy* average,
  not an arithmetic mean of dB:
  `Lnight = 10 * log10(mean(10 ^ (L_i / 10)))`.
  In Tiger, average `power(10, db / 10)` and convert back with `10 * log10(...)`.
- **City estimate:** per sensor, the energy average of nightly Lnight over at least the last 30
  nights. Fewer than 30 nights: show the sensor as "not enough data", don't shade it.
- **WHO road-traffic curve** (Basner & McGuire 2018), % highly sleep disturbed:
  `%HSD = 19.4312 - 0.9336 * Lnight + 0.0126 * Lnight^2`.
  This reproduces the plan's figures (2.9% at 45 dB, 6.2% at 55 dB, 8.8% at 60 dB). Still check
  the paper before quoting more decimals.
- **Valid range:** 40 to 65 dB Lnight. Outside it, clamp for shading and mark the value as
  out of range; never extrapolate.
- **Thresholds** (WHO 2018): night-time road traffic below 45 dB Lnight, rail 44 dB, aircraft
  40 dB.
- **Limits:** the curve is for long-term road-traffic noise at a home's most exposed facade.
  Observatory sensors sit at the kerb and also pick up nightlife and voices. So the map is an
  *indicative road-traffic estimate*, never a measured disturbance rate.

## Bedroom noise (phone)
- The iPhone microphone is not calibrated. Store and show **relative dB** only.
- Sample once a second. A **spike** is a level above the night's own baseline (rolling median)
  by a threshold set in `packages/shared`. Keep a 10-second clip around each spike.
- On-device voice-activity check: any clip containing speech is dropped on the phone and never
  uploaded.

## Wake-up attribution
- **Wake-up signals:** a Watch "awake" stage during the sleep session, or a sudden heart-rate
  jump during sleep (Watch stages are coarse and miss brief arousals).
- **Method:** look for a spike in the 60 to 120 seconds before each wake-up, and compare the hit
  rate against randomly chosen windows of the same length from the same night.
- **Small numbers:** one night has 2 to 6 wake-ups. Show counts ("3 of 4 wake-ups followed a
  spike"). Show a percentage only once several nights are pooled from HealthKit history.
- HealthKit sleep stages appear only after the sleep session ends. Live demo mode needs no Watch
  data.

## Noise classification
- Labels: `construction`, `traffic`, `siren`, `snoring`, `other`, plus `uncertain` and `handling`.
- **Handling noise** is the phone itself: rubbing on a sleeve, a pocket, a pillow or bedsheets.
  Kip's own small model (trained by us, see `ml/`) runs on each spike clip before Gemini. A clip
  that is mostly handling noise is labelled `handling`; otherwise the model's cleaned audio goes on
  to labelling. `handling` events are never linked to wake-ups and never appear in a briefing.
- Clips travel as 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV, so the server needs no audio decoder.
- Gemini (paid-tier key) labels each clip, with JSON output. ElevenLabs Scribe audio-event tags
  give a second opinion. Where they disagree, the event is `uncertain`. This stops a user's own
  snoring being blamed on the building site.
- The clip is deleted once labelled. Only the label is kept.

## Construction hours (Newcastle City Council)
Recommended hours for noisy construction work:

| Day | Allowed |
|---|---|
| Monday to Friday | 08:00 to 18:00 |
| Saturday | 08:00 to 13:00 |
| Sunday and bank holidays | None |

A `construction` event outside these hours is flagged "outside council hours". Bank holidays for
England come from `https://www.gov.uk/bank-holidays.json` (`england-and-wales`). These are
*recommended* hours: say "outside the council's recommended hours", not "illegal".

## Street Manager
DfT Street Manager pushes street and road works permits in England (location, work category,
traffic management type, proposed and actual times) over AWS SNS to a public HTTPS endpoint. The
subscription must be confirmed within 3 days. It covers roads, not building or demolition sites.
Night work is inferred from proposed times and traffic management type.

## Evidence log and Solana
Each night's log is serialised canonically, hashed (SHA-256), and the hash written to Solana
mainnet with the Memo program (no Anchor). It proves *when* a log existed, not that its contents
are true. Never claim more.

12	
13	### Intent
14	
15	AI-generated and template-driven UI converges on the same clichés: rainbow buttons, frosted glass panels, cartoon empty states, and decorative chrome that adds no function. This skill bans those patterns so interfaces stay purposeful, readable, and aligned with the rest of the visual-taste skills.
16	
17	### Hard Rules (Non-Negotiable)
18	
19	- **No multi-color radial rainbow gradients on standard CTA buttons.** Primary actions use a solid fill or a single-hue subtle gradient (same hue, ≤10% lightness shift). Ban `conic-gradient`, multi-stop rainbow `linear-gradient`, and purple-to-orange radial fills on default buttons.
20	- **No glassmorphic blur (`backdrop-filter`) without high-contrast boundary.** If blur is used at all, the panel must have a visible 1px border ≥3:1 against whatever shows through, opaque fallback when `backdrop-filter` unsupported, and sufficient text contrast. Default product UI should omit blur entirely.
21	- **No generic cartoon vector people** (waving, high-fiving, empty-box mascots) in empty states. Use text, actionable CTAs, simple monochrome icons, or product-relevant screenshots — not stock illustration people.
22	- **No icons inside inputs unless functional.** Allowed: search magnifier, clear/reset control, password visibility toggle. Banned: decorative leading icons on every text field, emoji-style adorners, brand icons inside standard inputs.
23	- **No unnecessary pill containers around standard text metadata.** Timestamps, author names, file sizes, and tags render as plain text or minimal chips only when they are interactive filters. Do not wrap static metadata in rounded pastel pills for decoration.
24	- **Anti-slop deletes decoration, not structure.** Remove pills, glass, cartoons, and decorative chrome. Do **not** delete the list frame, row dividers, or search chrome. An empty-looking table after a slop pass is a **fail**, not a pass.
25	
26	### Design Heuristics & Taste Principles
27	
28	- When a element's only job is decoration, delete it.
29	- Prefer one neutral border and whitespace over gradients, blobs, and floating shapes.
30	- Empty states sell the next action, not illustration budget.
31	- If it appears in a generic SaaS landing template, assume it is slop until proven functional.
32	- Cross-check `.ux-profile.md` banned list — it may extend these rules.
33	
34	### Concrete Scenarios (Before vs. After)
35	
36	#### ❌ Anti-Pattern
37	
38	Sign-up uses a `conic-gradient` "Get Started" button. Login form inputs each have a leading gray icon. Empty project view shows a cartoon character high-fiving. Settings show "Last updated" inside a lavender pill. A modal uses `backdrop-filter: blur(20px)` with no border on a busy background.
39	
40	#### ✅ Best Practice
41	
42	Primary CTA is solid accent fill. Search field keeps one magnifier icon; other fields are label + input only. Empty state: heading, one sentence of value, "Create project" button, optional simple 24px monochrome icon. Metadata runs as 12px secondary text. Modal uses opaque L3 surface, 1px border, optional scrim — no blur.
